newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's INCA to launch 500 mln rand bonds in Feb.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's INCA to launch 500 mln rand bonds in Feb.

text.p: South Africa's Infrastructure Finance Corp (INCA), set up last October, will issue 500 million rand of bonds via a private placing on February 11, managing direct Johan Kruger said on Thursday.
The 13.5-percent, 10-year bonds will be listed on the Bond Exchange of South Africa from February 21.
INCA, established to help fund infrastructure projects throughout South Africa, announced at the time of its launch that it intended to raise 1.2 billion rand from investors in 1997.

Kruger said further issues later in the year would comprise another issue for 300 million rand of 13.5-percent, 10-year bonds, 200 million rand of 13.5-percent, five-year bonds and 200 million rand of 14-percent, 15-year bonds.
It was too early to give a timetable for these further issues, he told Reuters.
In total, INCA intends to raise 12 billion rand over the next seven years in a process that will see the private sector joining government in addressing the country's massive infrastructure backlog.
Government estimates put South Africa's total infrastruture needs at 171 billion rand over the next five years.

INCA, which has a domestic long-term rating of AA- from European rating agency IBCA, will use funds raised by the bond issues to provide debt financing at low rates of interest to all infrastructure providers, ranging from local authorities, water utilities and municipalities to private infrastructure companies.

Principal partners in INCA are First National Bank, the Commonwealth Development Corp and Southern Life, each with 20 percent. Other shareholders include Msele Ltd, Old Mutual and Women Investment Portfolio.
